candidates.name: Myocarditis
support_spans: a high-sensitivity troponin T of 275 ng/L (<14) peaking at 632 ng/L on hospital day 2
extensive patchy late gadolinium enhancement in a mid-wall to epicardial distribution, particularly in the basal and mid lateral wall
T2-weighted imaging suggested myocardial edema
candidates.why: The patient's presentation with chest pain, elevated troponin levels, and CMR findings of myocardial edema and late gadolinium enhancement are consistent with myocarditis.

candidates.name: Acute Coronary Syndrome
support_spans: a high-sensitivity troponin T of 275 ng/L (<14) peaking at 632 ng/L on hospital day 2
contradict_spans: On examination he was hemodynamically stable

Transthoracic echocardiography showed a normal left ventricular size, borderline low systolic function (LVEF 50–55%) with dyssynchronous septal motion, and a normal right ventricle without pericardial effusion
candidates.why: The patient's elevated troponin levels could suggest acute coronary syndrome, but the lack of other typical symptoms and the CMR findings make this less likely.

candidates.name: Pericarditis

contradict_spans: There was no pericardial enhancement or effusion
candidates.why: The patient's pleuritic chest pain could suggest pericarditis, but the lack of pericardial effusion or enhancement on CMR makes this less likely.
